subject: Learning Methods
title: Using Notes for Self-Testing
description: A short lesson to help you apply Using Notes for Self-Testing.

hook.text: He used his Cornell notes as flashcards: covered the right column and quizzed himself from the cue questions.

buildup.text: Notes with questions built in become self-testing tools. The testing effect makes this far more powerful than rereading.

discovery.text: Any note format can support self-testing if you add questions during review. Cornell bakes this in by design.

twist.text: Rereading notes feels productive but is mostly passive. Self-testing feels harder but produces two to three times.

climax.text: After reviewing notes, close them and write everything you remember from memory. Check and fill gaps.

punchline.text: Don't reread notes. Quiz yourself from them. Triple the effect.

quiz.question: Why does self-testing from notes outperform rereading?
options: It takes less time than rereading
Retrieval practice produces two to three times better retention
Self-testing is more enjoyable than rereading
